title: Dutch Oven Pot Roast
seoTitle: Dutch Oven Pot Roast | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Chuck roast with carrots and potatoes braised for ten
subtitle: Chuck roast with carrots and potatoes braised for ten
description: Beef chuck sears in a Dutch oven, then braises low with broth, tomato paste, and aromatics until fork-tender. Carrots and potatoes cook in the same pot for a complete meal.

steps.title: Sear the roast
steps.instruction: Pat chuck dry and season generously. Sear in oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat 3–4 minutes per side until deeply browned. Set aside.

steps.title: Build the braise
steps.instruction: Sauté onion and garlic 3 minutes. Stir in tomato paste and cook 1 minute. Add broth, Worcestershire, and thyme, scraping fond from the bottom.

steps.title: Braise low and slow
steps.instruction: Return roast to pot, cover, and braise at 325°F until fork-tender and internal temp reaches 203°F, about 2.5–3 hours. Target oven/smoker temperature: 325°F.

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.instruction: Nestle potatoes and carrots around roast. Cover and continue braising at 325°F until vegetables pierce easily, about 60–75 minutes. Target oven/smoker temperature: 325°F.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.instruction: Rest roast 15 minutes. Whisk flour slurry into simmering braising liquid for gravy. Slice or shred beef and serve with vegetables and gravy.

proTips: Do not skip the sear—gray pot roast tastes flat no matter how long it braises.
If gravy is thin, simmer uncovered 10 minutes before adding slurry.
Celery stalks added with carrots deepen the savory base cheaply.
tonightSpread: Sliced pot roast with gravy, potatoes, and carrots on platters.
Crusty bread for soaking up extra gravy at the end of the line.
leftovers: Shred leftovers for French dip sandwiches with strained gravy.
Dice into a beef and vegetable soup with leftover braising liquid.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Pot roast is the definition of hall comfort—fork-tender beef, rich gravy, and vegetables in one pot. It holds warm for late eaters and tastes better the next day.
mealPrepNotes: Sear roast hard for deep color before braising. Cut vegetables large so they do not turn to mush. Shred or slice roast after resting 15 minutes.

adaptable.label: Gluten-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use a certified gluten-free broth or bouillon. Use a certified gluten-free Worcestershire sauce. Use a 1:1 gluten-free all-purpose flour blend.
